data.description:
## Why

108 tickets in the store carry `## Success Criteria`. Their criteria are conventionally plain
`- ` bullets, and `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under `## Acceptance Criteria`
(resetting at the next `##`). So those criteria are invisible to the P1 blocking floor, cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag the completion verifier matches on checkbox text, and are
not individually checkable. Migrating them is the substantive half of this epic — the heading
rename is cosmetic by comparison.

## What

Migrate the store tickets carrying `## Success Criteria` so their criteria live under
`## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items.

## Scope

The ticket descriptions in the `tickets` branch that match `## Success Criteria` (108 distinct
tickets at time of writing; the migration recomputes the set rather than hard-coding it).

A migration script under `scripts/` performing the rewrite via the rebar library
(`rebar.edit_ticket`) so every change is a normal, auditable ticket event — NOT a direct
rewrite of the git-backed store.

OUT OF SCOPE: closed tickets' historical accuracy is not preserved by rewriting; see Approach
for why closed tickets are migrated too and what that costs.

## Approach

For each matching ticket: locate the `## Success Criteria` block (bounded by the next `## `
heading), convert its `- ` bullets to `- [ ]` items, and merge them into the ticket's existing
`## Acceptance Criteria` block, appending if one exists and creating it if not. Tickets already
carrying both headings merge; the SC heading is then removed.

Editing a ticket's description changes its MATERIAL FINGERPRINT, which invalidates any
plan-review attestation as `stale-material`. That is correct and unavoidable — the plan text
genuinely changed — but it means the migration must not be run blindly across claimed work.
The script therefore processes CLOSED tickets by default and requires an explicit flag to touch
open/in_progress ones, so no in-flight claim is silently invalidated. The count of skipped
in-flight tickets is reported so the remainder can be migrated deliberately.

Run as a dry-run first, with the diff recorded on this ticket before the live run.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the block-rewriting function over fixtures: SC-only, both-headings, SC with
  mixed `- ` and `- [ ]` items, SC as the LAST section (no following `##`), and a ticket with
  no SC block (must be a no-op).
- Dry-run over the real store, with the resulting diff attached as a ticket comment.
- Post-migration assertion that `_count_ac_items` returns >=1 for every migrated ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A script under `scripts/` performs the migration through `rebar.edit_ticket`, with
      `--dry-run` as the default mode and a required explicit flag to modify non-closed tickets.
- [ ] Unit tests cover all five block-shape cases listed under Testing, including the no-op case.
- [ ] After the live run, `git grep -l "## Success Criteria" tickets` matches no ticket
      description outside the skipped in-flight set.
- [ ] Every migrated ticket returns `_count_ac_items >= 1`, verified by a script pass over the
      migrated set.
- [ ] The dry-run diff and the list of skipped in-flight tickets are recorded as comments on
      this ticket.
data.title: Rewrite author guide and user docs for the collapsed criteria vocabulary
